reasons: Rule application is sound: the take-or-pay commitment survives 'without reduction or termination rights', so it operates as a Customer-payable minimum charge on termination/reduced usage, which falls within the LD rule's detection guidance (minimum fees on termination, amounts due irrespective of Services taken).

Direction is correct and pro-Customer: the redline removes the USD 2,000,000/yr (up to USD 6,000,000) exposure rather than merely narrowing it, matching the preferred position of no liquidated damages or penalties payable by Customer.

The high changed-character ratio is justified here — the playbook requires deletion of the whole commitment, and the replacement sentence is a clean substitute rather than an unrelated rewrite; the added 'no LD/penalty/early-termination fee/minimum charge' language is broader than a bare deletion but stays within the preferred position.

Comment is accurate, concise, in the required voice and prefix, explains the 'without reduction or termination rights' trigger, notes the internal conflicts, and offers the 3-months'-fees early-termination-fee fallback.
